About

Ebin Sebastian

Physical chemist and ultrafast spectroscopist at the Cavendish Laboratory, University of Cambridge, working with Prof. Akshay Rao since 2022, including two years as an MSCA–UKRI Postdoctoral Fellow. PhD in Chemistry, IISER Thiruvananthapuram, 2022.

Read more

Research

Molecular design, ultrafast spectroscopy and excited-state theory

How does molecular organisation control energy flow and the fate of excited states?

After a molecule absorbs light, its arrangement relative to its neighbours decides whether the energy becomes free charges, pairs of triplet excitons, or is lost. I address this question by combining three approaches.

  • Molecular design and assembly

    Chromophores and assemblies with controlled coupling, spacing and packing.

    Bichromophore synthesis; supramolecular assembly for thin-film morphology

  • Ultrafast spectroscopy

    Excited states followed from femtoseconds to microseconds.

    Transient absorption, time-resolved photoluminescence, IVS and GHOST

  • Excited-state theory

    Calculations that link measured spectra to structure and coupling.

    DFT, TD-DFT and multi-reference methods; vibronic and Spano analyses

Research areas

Select an area to read more.

Where this is going

My independent research programme asks how molecular organisation can be engineered to control energy transport from molecular to mesoscopic length scales. It will combine molecular design, ultrafast spectroscopy, transient microscopy and structural characterisation to connect local excited-state dynamics with long-range material function.

Mentoring, supervision and the collaborations behind the work

Biography

I am a physical chemist and ultrafast spectroscopist in the group of Prof. Akshay Rao at the Cavendish Laboratory, University of Cambridge, where I have worked since 2022, including two years as a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA)–UKRI Postdoctoral Fellow on an independently developed proposal.

I completed my PhD in Chemistry in 2022 at IISER Thiruvananthapuram, India, with Prof. Mahesh Hariharan, working on orthogonal bichromophoric systems from null excitonic coupling to symmetry-breaking charge separation.
